correctness.rationale: Singleton factors force q markers and the first full period is an attractor. When m=1, a factor either meets a letter occurring once or is contained in both copies of the short prefix. For m≥2, an unwrapped short factor contains a symbol all of whose copies lie in its occurrence union. A wrapped short factor whose wrapped tail fits the appended prefix hits every q−1; otherwise its occurrence union excludes q−1 only in the last full period, r only in the initial period, and j<r only in the two boundary copies. For length at least q, successive occurrences touch or overlap; the missed markers must lie in two end segments of length <q. The right segment must contain the last q−1, which forces it not to contain r; the same restrictions follow. They are inconsistent when r=q−1 and m≥2. For r≤q−2 the literal factor (q−1)0…r has starts q,2q,…,(m−1)q and misses exactly the stated pattern. Independent literal occurrence-union enumeration (python3 /workspace/branches/reproduce.py 4) reproduced 88 cases, 52,430 candidates and 835 failures; the proof, not the census, handles the unbounded parameters. The common witness need not be the only factor a choice misses.
